from marimo._ast.app import InternalApp
from marimo._ast.load import load_notebook_ir
from marimo._runtime.dataflow import topological_sort
from marimo._schemas.serialization import NotebookSerialization
from marimo._version import __version__


def _header_for_script(ir: NotebookSerialization) -> str:
    """Extract a Python script-appropriate header from the notebook IR.

    For Python-origin notebooks, ``ir.header.value`` holds the raw header text
    (which may contain a PEP 723 ``# /// script`` block and copyright
    comments), which is returned verbatim. For Markdown-origin notebooks,
    ``ir.header.value`` holds YAML frontmatter; the PEP 723 header is
    reconstructed from its ``pyproject`` or ``header`` keys. Returns an empty
    string when the IR has no header.
    """
    if ir.header is None or not ir.header.value:
        return ""

    import yaml

    from marimo._utils.inline_script_metadata import (
        get_headers_from_frontmatter,
    )

    header_value = ir.header.value

    # Markdown-origin notebooks store YAML frontmatter in the header, whereas
    # Python-origin notebooks store raw comment text. Raw comment text parses
    # to ``None`` under YAML, so a dict result signals a Markdown origin.
    try:
        frontmatter = yaml.safe_load(header_value)
    except yaml.YAMLError:
        frontmatter = None

    if isinstance(frontmatter, dict):
        headers = get_headers_from_frontmatter(frontmatter)
        return headers["pyproject"] or headers["header"]

    return header_value


def convert_from_ir_to_script(ir: NotebookSerialization) -> str:
    app = InternalApp(load_notebook_ir(ir))

    # Check if any code is async, if so, raise an error
    for cell in app.cell_manager.cells():
        if not cell:
            continue
        if cell._is_coroutine:
            from click import ClickException

            raise ClickException(
                "Cannot export a notebook with async code to a flat script"
            )

    graph = app.graph
    header = _header_for_script(ir)
    codes: list[str] = [
        "# %%\n" + graph.cells[cid].code
        for cid in topological_sort(graph, graph.cells.keys())
    ]
    return f'{header}\n__generated_with = "{__version__}"\n\n' + "\n\n".join(
        codes
    )
